@Suhaan asked me to take a look at https://github.com/entirehq/entire-api/pull/299 https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1763

I see some issues with this approach too.


Yes, the CLI should not ship with hardcoded agents/models/costs but instead load them from an API. Like ideally the CLI caches the remote data once per day in a global place per machine. 
Always calculating on the backend has an issue because model prices change. This does not always happen but it does. My understanding is that what entire-api calculates is not treated as persistent data but instead something that can be rebuild. But even if it is, a fork or a repo pushed to a completely new repo name (without any fork reference) would mean we would calculate with what ever data we have at that day OR need to keep historic pricing. So I feel calculating it in the checkpoint metadata does make some sense :thinking_face:


Happy to hear other thoughts on this.

Yes. +1 on 1. And to be fair, if we would want to we could still do both, like we could re-calculate anytime anywhere, it would just require the prices at the time but it's much better to do it directly on the session and write to the metadata as it reduces the complexity by a fair bit.
[8:45 AM]I'd suggest pointing an agent to the Pi implementation and compare against what we have. What they have seems to work pretty reliable and I assume it's pretty much doing what you say in 1.
soph  [9:57 AM]
Layer 1: baked into the build

packages/ai/package.json:57 — build runs generate-models before compiling, so every publish re-fetches models.dev and regenerates the per-provider catalogs (src/providers/*.models.ts, src/providers/data/). That directory is gitignored (.gitignore:11) and hydrated at build time, then copied into dist. So the npm tarball carries a pricing snapshot frozen at publish time, stamped with generatedAt in src/providers/data/.manifest.json.

Layer 2: a runtime overlay from pi.dev

packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts wraps every built-in provider (except radius) in withRemoteCatalog, which:

- fetches https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/{id} at most every 4 hours (REMOTE_CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS, line 7)
- revalidates with ETag / if-none-match, persists the body to models-store.json
- merges by model id — remote entries replace same-id built-ins, new ids get appended (mergeModels, line 9)

The staleness guard is the interesting bit (remoteModels, line 33-42): the overlay is discarded entirely if the remote catalog's last-modified is older than or equal to the shipped build's generatedAt. So a freshly published pi always wins over a stale pi.dev catalog, and the overlay only ever moves pricing forward. Failure modes are conservative too — a non-OK response keeps the cached body and etag, a 404/501 pins lastModified: 0 so the overlay stays inert.

That pi.dev catalog comes from the same generator: npm run generate:model-catalog writes to .artifacts/model-catalog, and scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs uploads it to a bucket with a MINIMUM_PI_VERSION gate (currently 0.80.7) and sanity checks (≥500 models, anthropic/openai/openrouter present).

The practical consequence

Pricing errors are correctable without a release — push a new catalog to pi.dev and clients pick it up within 4 hours. But an offline client, or one whose build is newer than the published catalog, prices from the tarball snapshot. And since cost is computed locally rather than read from the provider's response, any drift between models.dev and actual provider billing shows up silently as wrong numbers in the footer — nothing reconciles against a real invoice.[9:57 AM]tl;dr pi ships with prices but also refreshs them every 4h

input.description: Research cli PR #1763 in depth
input.prompt:
Research entireio/cli PR #1763 ("refactor(cost): CLI stops storing cost; platform owns it (supersedes #1702)") using `gh` CLI (assume gh is authenticated).

Context you need: This PR removes CLI-side cost calculation, deferring cost computation to the platform (entire-api PR #299, which computes cost server-side from raw model_usage). A Slack thread among the team (soph, dipree, ashtom, Suhaan) raised concerns about this direction:
- CLI currently ships hardcoded model/agent/cost tables — bad because prices change and go stale.
- Computing cost purely server-side has a problem: a forked/renamed repo with no fork-lineage would get costed using whatever pricing data exists on that day, with no way to recover historical pricing for old sessions — unless historic pricing is retained. dipree argued it's simpler to compute cost client-side (in the CLI) AT SESSION TIME and write the computed cost into the checkpoint metadata directly, rather than relying on the backend to recompute after the fact.
- The team also looked at how the Pi coding agent (earendil-works/pi, npm packages/coding-agent + packages/ai) handles this: it ships a baked-in pricing snapshot from models.dev at build time, PLUS a runtime overlay that refetches from pi.dev at most every 4 hours with ETag revalidation and a staleness guard (discard overlay if remote's last-modified <= build's generatedAt).

Your job — pure research, no code changes:
1. Run `gh pr view 1763 --repo entireio/cli --json title,body,author,state,baseRefName,headRefName,commits,reviews,comments,files` (or similar) to get metadata, description, current review state/comments.
2. Run `gh pr diff 1763 --repo entireio/cli` to get the full diff. Summarize precisely: what files changed, what cost-calculation logic was REMOVED from the CLI (function names, file paths, line numbers), what replaced it (e.g. does it now just pass raw token counts / model_usage without any $ cost?), and what checkpoint metadata schema changes were made.
3. Check `gh pr view 1763 --repo entireio/cli --comments` for any review comments/discussion on GitHub itself (separate from the Slack thread).
4. Identify: does this PR touch any model/agent pricing table files currently hardcoded in the CLI (e.g. something like internal/*/pricing.go, models.json, a models catalog)? Find and note their exact paths, even if the PR doesn't touch them — I need to know where hardcoded pricing currently lives in the cli repo today (check main branch, not just the PR diff) so we can determine what "the CLI ships hardcoded agents/models/costs" refers to concretely. Use `entire graph search` or grep if needed against a local checkout (check if `/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli-1702` or `/Users/suhaan/devenv/cli/` exists locally and has this code; if not, fetch via gh api or clone shallow to a scratch dir under /private/tmp/claude-501/... — do NOT touch /Users/suhaan/devenv/cli/ main checkout, read-only is fine there if it exists).
5. Note who authored #1763 (soph? someone else?) and whether Suhaan (the user) is a collaborator/reviewer on it.
6. Note the exact current HEAD commit SHA of the PR branch and the branch name, so we can `gh pr checkout` it later if needed.

Report back (compressed, dense, no fluff — this feeds an architectural decision, not a demo):
- PR metadata (author, branch name, head SHA, state, base branch)
- Concrete before/after of what the diff does to cost calculation (file:line level)
- Exact current location(s) of hardcoded model/agent/pricing data in the cli repo (file paths)
- Any GitHub-side review comments not already covered by the Slack thread
- Anything that looks like WIP/incomplete/TODO in the diff relevant to this cost-ownership question

Keep the report under 600 words, dense with file:line references.

input.description: Research entire-api PR #299 in depth
input.prompt:
Research entirehq/entire-api PR #299 ("feat(cost): compute cost on the platform from model_usage (supersedes #261)") using `gh` CLI (assume gh is authenticated).

Context you need: This PR makes entire-api (the Go backend, per-jurisdiction "cell" service) compute the dollar cost of an AI coding session server-side from raw model_usage records (tokens per model), rather than trusting a pre-computed cost value written by the CLI. A Slack thread among the team (soph, dipree, ashtom, Suhaan) raised concerns:
- Backend-only cost calculation has a staleness/history problem: if pricing data used at calculation time is "whatever we have that day," and a repo is forked/renamed without fork-lineage, there's no way to know what price applied at the time tokens were actually spent, unless the backend keeps a full historical pricing table indexed by date.
- dipree argued computing cost client-side (CLI, at session time) and writing it directly into checkpoint metadata is simpler and avoids needing to reconstruct historical pricing later.
- The team discussed sourcing pricing data from models.dev (github.com/anomalyco/models.dev, git-backed, could give price history "for free" via commit history) and/or building their own API that serves a model/pricing catalog (ashtom: "Just make an API on our end that provides the data to our CLI" — also floated selling this catalog+history to customers).
- They also researched how Pi (earendil-works/pi) does it: build-time snapshot from models.dev + runtime refresh from pi.dev every 4h with staleness guards.

Your job — pure research, no code changes:
1. Run `gh pr view 299 --repo entirehq/entire-api --json title,body,author,state,baseRefName,headRefName,commits,reviews,comments,files` for metadata/description/review state.
2. Run `gh pr diff 299 --repo entirehq/entire-api` for the full diff. Summarize precisely: what tables/migrations were added (look for goose migrations `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql` under repo store), what Go code computes cost from model_usage (file:line, function names), where the pricing table/constants live in this PR (is it hardcoded Go constants? a config file? fetched from somewhere?), and whether there's any versioning/history mechanism for pricing already present.
3. Check `gh pr view 299 --repo entirehq/entire-api --comments` for GitHub-side review discussion.
4. Note whether this PR or the current entire-api main branch has ANY existing model/pricing catalog data or endpoint (search for "pricing", "model_usage", "cost", "catalog" in the repo). Check if `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api-261` or `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api/` exist locally (read-only, do not modify) and use them if present; otherwise use `gh api` / shallow clone to a scratch dir under /private/tmp/claude-501/... — never touch /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api/ main checkout beyond reading.
5. Note the exact current HEAD commit SHA and branch name of PR #299, and its author, and whether it references or replaces PR #261 explicitly (commit messages, PR body).
6. Check if entire-api already has any public/CLI-facing API route (`/api/v1/*`) that could naturally serve a "models catalog" — note existing route file structure (per CODEBASE-MAP.md, cmd/api handles `/api/v1/*`) so we know where a new catalog endpoint would slot in.

Report back (compressed, dense — feeds an architectural decision):
- PR metadata (author, branch, head SHA, state, base)
- Concrete summary of the cost-from-model_usage computation (file:line), migrations added
- Exact current pricing-constant location(s) in this PR / repo
- Any existing catalog/models API surface, or nearest existing route pattern to extend
- GitHub-side review comments not covered by Slack
- Anything WIP/incomplete relevant to pricing history/versioning

Keep the report under 600 words, dense with file:line references.

Research the earendil-works/pi GitHub repo's model pricing/catalog system in concrete implementation detail, to serve as a reference for reimplementing something similar in Anthropic's internal "Entire" CLI (Go) and backend (Go/Postgres). This is for legitimate reference/reimplementation — Pi is MIT licensed and the team has already discussed reusing its approach.

A colleague already summarized the high level (paste for your context):
- Layer 1 (build-time): packages/ai/package.json build runs a `generate-models` script before compiling; it fetches models.dev and regenerates per-provider catalogs into packages/ai/src/providers/*.models.ts and src/providers/data/ (gitignored, hydrated at build time, copied into the npm dist). Stamped with `generatedAt` in src/providers/data/.manifest.json.
- Layer 2 (runtime overlay): packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts wraps every built-in provider (except "radius") in `withRemoteCatalog`, which fetches https://pi.dev/api/models/providers/{id} at most every 4 hours (REMOTE_CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS), revalidates with ETag/if-none-match, persists response body to models-store.json, merges by model id (mergeModels — remote replaces same-id built-ins, appends new ids). Staleness guard: overlay discarded entirely if remote catalog's last-modified <= build's generatedAt (so a fresh build always beats a stale remote catalog; overlay only moves pricing forward, never backward). Failure modes: non-OK response keeps cached body/etag; 404/501 pins lastModified:0 so overlay stays inert.
- The pi.dev catalog itself is produced by `npm run generate:model-catalog` (writes to .artifacts/model-catalog) and `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs` uploads it to a bucket with a MINIMUM_PI_VERSION gate and sanity checks (>=500 models, anthropic/openai/openrouter present).
- Reference commit for generate-models.ts: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/d1a305613ea6f9e5d5ddc9e08f27393f9b73b33c/packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts (line ~2256 is where `generateModels()` starts)

Your job:
1. Fetch the actual source of these files from GitHub (use WebFetch on raw.githubusercontent.com URLs, or `gh api repos/earendil-works/pi/contents/<path>` if you have gh access to that public repo) at commit d1a305613ea6f9e5d5ddc9e08f27393f9b73b33c (or latest main if that SHA 404s):
   - packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts (focus on generateModels() and how it derives pricing fields, and how it decides model id / provider grouping)
   - packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts (full file)
   - packages/ai/src/providers/data/.manifest.json (structure — may not exist as a checked-in file since gitignored; if not found, note that)
   - scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs
   - Any script under packages/ai that does `generate:model-catalog` (find via package.json scripts)
2. Also fetch github.com/anomalyco/models.dev's data schema — specifically find one provider's pricing JSON/data file (e.g. anthropic.json or similar) to see exact field names for input/output/cache-read/cache-write token pricing, and effective-date fields if any exist.
3. Extract the EXACT data shape (JSON schema / TS interface) used for: a single model's pricing entry (input cost per token, output cost per token, cache read/write costs, context window, etc.), and the wire format of the /api/models/providers/{id} response.
4. Extract the exact staleness-guard algorithm (the real code, not paraphrase) from remote-catalog-provider.ts, and the exact refresh-interval / ETag / cache-file persistence logic.

Report back (dense, code-forward — this is a reimplementation reference, include real field names and real code snippets for the staleness guard and the pricing data shape, but keep total under 900 words):
- Exact pricing entry schema (field names + types)
- Exact staleness-guard + refresh logic (small code excerpt, not full file dumps)
- Exact catalog-generation pipeline (script names, inputs/outputs, gates)
- models.dev's raw data schema for one example model
- Any date/effective-pricing versioning already present in models.dev's schema (the Slack thread specifically wondered whether commit-date can be trusted as the price-change date, or whether an explicit date field exists in the data)

**Cost computation (file:line):**
- `internal/ingest/cost.go:1-55` — `estimateCost(model string, tu tokenUsage) *float64` loads embedded table via `sync.OnceValues(pricing.LoadTable(nil))`, does `tbl.Lookup(model)`, calls `pricing.Estimate(rate, usage)`; unknown model → nil (never a guess/fallback).
- `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go` `parseSession` (~line 593-620ish per diff) — iterates `metadata.json`'s `model_usage` array, calls `estimateCost` per bucket, sums into session cost, stamps `cost_source="estimated"`; **CLI-supplied `cost_usd`/`cost_source` fields are parsed but discarded** ("platform is the source of truth").
- `buildCheckpointRow` (~line 652-690) — checkpoint cost = sum of session costs; `CollapseCostSource` handles multi-source aggregation.
- `applySessionCost` (~line 769+) — sanitizes summed cost via `store.SanitizeCost`.

**Migrations:** `internal/store/migrations/repo/051_checkpoint_session_cost.sql` (renumbered from 049 after colliding with main's 049/050 — noted in the 2026-07-16 update as the migration's **2nd renumber**; author flagged main now mandates UTC-timestamp migration filenames but kept an integer) and `internal/store/migrations/user/009_my_activity_cost.sql`. Both add `cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6)` + `cost_source TEXT` with a `NOT VALID` CHECK constraint (`reported`/`estimated`/`mixed`), no DEFAULT (NULL = "no cost reported," distinct from real $0).

**Pricing table location — confirms the Slack staleness concern is real and unaddressed in-code:** `internal/pricing/models/{anthropic,openai,google,cursor}.json`, compiled in via `go:embed` (`internal/pricing/embed.go`). Each `ModelRate` (`internal/pricing/table.go`) has a single `EffectiveDate string` field — **informational only, not indexed/queryable by date**. `Table.Lookup(model)` and `Estimate(rate, usage)` take **no `asOf` timestamp** — there is exactly one current rate per model, no history array, no way to price a checkpoint at the rate that applied when tokens were actually spent. This is a straight port of the CLI's pricing engine (`internal/pricing/doc.go`), self-contained, no cross-repo dep.

**Versioning/freshness mechanism added in review response (2026-07-16):** `mise run pricing:check` (diffs tracked models against LiteLLM's `model_prices_and_context_window.json`, reports drift, non-zero exit) and `mise run pricing:update -write` (applies matchable updates, bumps `effective_date`) — implemented in `internal/pricing/pricingcheck/main.go` (496 lines). Provenance doc `internal/pricing/models/SOURCE.md`. This is explicitly called a **stopgap**; PR body's "Follow-ups" section says **Phase 3** (server-side live pricing pull — "a pricing git repo + `git pull`, per jdx, is lighter than a JSON API" — plus a re-price job over stored token buckets) is **not in this PR** ("No pricing-source live-refresh in this PR (embedded table only)").

**No existing catalog/models API surface:** searched `entirehq/entire-api` main (shallow clone) for `pricing`/`catalog`/`models` route — none exists. Route convention (confirmed via `internal/httpapi/router.go:79` `const APIBase = "/api/v1"` and per-feature files like `preferences.go` using `huma.Register` for e.g. `/preferences/*`) means a new models/pricing-catalog endpoint would naturally slot in as its own `internal/httpapi/models_catalog.go` (or `pricing.go`) file registering under `/api/v1/models` or `/api/v1/pricing`, same pattern as `preferences.go`/`experts.go`/`admin.go`.

**Known findings called out in PR body itself:** (1) dual precision — checkpoint `cost_usd` NUMERIC(14,6) vs per-model JSONB full float, sums can mismatch by sub-cent; (2) cost is load-bearing on `model_usage[].model` — a checkpoint with aggregate tokens but no resolvable per-model bucket gets nil cost, stricter than the old CLI-computed design.</result>

<result>## Findings: earendil-works/pi model pricing/catalog system

All fetched at pinned commit `d1a305613ea6f9e5d5ddc9e08f27393f9b73b33c` (files exist there; `.manifest.json` is gitignored, confirmed 404).

### 1. Pricing entry schema (`packages/ai/src/types.ts:767-800`)

```ts
export interface ModelCostRates {
  input: number;      // $/million tokens
  output: number;     // $/million tokens
  cacheRead: number;  // $/million tokens
  cacheWrite: number; // $/million tokens
}
export interface ModelCostTier extends ModelCostRates {
  inputTokensAbove: number; // request-wide; highest matching threshold wins
}
export interface ModelCost extends ModelCostRates {
  tiers?: ModelCostTier[];
}
export interface Model<TApi extends Api> {
  id: string; name: string; api: TApi; provider: ProviderId; baseUrl: string;
  reasoning: boolean; thinkingLevelMap?: ThinkingLevelMap;
  input: ("text"|"image")[]; cost: ModelCost;
  contextWindow: number; maxTokens: number;
  samplingParams?: Record<string, unknown>; headers?: Record<string,string>;
  compat?: /* per-api compat union */;
}
```
No cost-history/effective-date field anywhere in this type. Flat current-value snapshot only.

### 2. Staleness guard + refresh (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts`, full file, 132 lines)

Core guard — a fresher build always wins, overlay only moves forward:
```ts
export const REMOTE_CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 4 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

function remoteModels(entry: ModelsStoreEntry | undefined, localGeneratedAt: number | undefined) {
  if (!entry) return [];
  if (localGeneratedAt !== undefined &&
      (entry.lastModified === undefined || entry.lastModified <= localGeneratedAt)) {
    return []; // overlay discarded entirely
  }
  return entry.models;
}
```
Refresh gate (in-window skip, ETag revalidation, 304/404/501/error handling):
```ts
if (!context.force && stored?.checkedAt !== undefined && stored.lastModified !== undefined &&
    Date.now() - stored.checkedAt < REMOTE_CATALOG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS) return;

const validator = stored?.models.length ? stored.etag : undefined; // only revalidate if a body backs it
const response = await fetchWithRetry(
  new URL(`/api/models/providers/${encodeURIComponent(provider.id)}`, catalogBaseUrl),
  { headers: { accept: "application/json", "User-Agent": getPiUserAgent(VERSION),
      ...(validator ? { "if-none-match": validator } : {}) }, signal: context.signal });

if (response.status === 304 && stored) { await context.publish({ persist: { ...stored, checkedAt } }); return; }
if (response.status === 404 || response.status === 501) {
  await context.publish({ persist: { ...(stored ?? {models:[]}), checkedAt, lastModified: 0, etag: undefined } });
  return; // pins lastModified:0 -> overlay stays inert forever until a real 200
}
if (!response.ok) { await context.publish({ persist: { ...(stored ?? {models:[]}), checkedAt } }); throw new Error(...); }

const refreshed = parseCatalog(provider.id, await response.json());
const lastModified = Date.parse(response.headers.get("last-modified") ?? "");
const entry = { models: refreshed, checkedAt, lastModified: Number.isNaN(lastModified)?0:lastModified,
                 etag: response.headers.get("etag") ?? undefined };
await context.publish({ persist: entry, update: () => { dynamicModels = remoteModels(entry, localGeneratedAt); } });
```
Merge: `mergeModels` overwrites by matching `id` (in place), appends new ids. Wire format tolerant: `parseCatalog` accepts a bare array, `{models:[...]}`, or an id→model map.

Cache file: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/models-store.ts` — `FileModelsStore` persists to `~/.../models-store.json` (one JSON blob keyed by providerId → `ModelsStoreEntry{models, lastModified?, checkedAt?, etag?}`), file-locked via `AuthStorageBackend.withLockAsync`, revision-cached by mtime to avoid redundant reparse across concurrent readers.

`localGeneratedAt` wiring (`packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts`): `Date.parse(modelDataManifest.generatedAt)` from the build's `.manifest.json`; passed into `withRemoteCatalog(provider, catalogBaseUrl, builtinModelDataGeneratedAt)` for every built-in provider except `radius` (`model-runtime.ts:186-188`).

### 3. Catalog-generation pipeline

- `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` `generateModels()` (line 2256): fetches `https://models.dev/api.json` (single JSON blob, all providers) + OpenRouter + Cloudflare AI Gateway, concatenates `[...modelsDev, ...openRouter, ...aiGateway]`, dedupes by `(provider, id)` first-write-wins (models.dev > OpenRouter > Gateway), then applies ~20 hardcoded per-model override blocks (context windows, cost overrides for specific ids like `z-ai/glm-5`). Grouped into `providers[providerId][modelId]`, sorted.
- Writes `src/providers/data/<providerId>.json` (grouped by api), then `src/providers/data/.manifest.json` via `createModelDataManifest`: `{schemaVersion:3, generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(), structureHash: sha256(sorted structure), files: {filename: sha256(content)}}` (`model-data.ts:127-138`).
- Generates `src/providers/<id>.models.ts` shards (`import values from "./data/<id>.json"`) + aggregator `src/models.generated.ts`. All staged in a temp dir, validated (`validateModelDataDirectory`), then atomically swapped in; a `restoreGeneratedCatalog` closure reverts on failure.
- CLI flags: `--strict`, `--data-only` (hydrate data only, no `.models.ts`), `--json-only --json-output <dir>` → npm script `generate-model-catalog` writes `.artifacts/model-catalog/{models.json, providers.json, providers/<id>.json}`.
- `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs`: `validateBundle()` gates — providers.json must equal sorted keys of models.json; each model's `id`/`provider` must match its shard slot; `REQUIRED_PROVIDERS=["anthropic","openai","openrouter"]` must exist; `MINIMUM_MODEL_COUNT=500`. Computes `revision = "sha256-" + sha256(models.json bytes)`. Uploads to S3-compatible bucket keys `models/v1/revisions/<revision>/{models.json,providers.json,providers/<id>.json}` (immutable cache-control), then rewrites `models/v1/index.json` (`no-store`), keyed by `MINIMUM_PI_VERSION` (currently `0.80.7`) — old entries for the same min-version are replaced, others preserved, sorted by version.

### 4. models.dev raw schema (live `claude-sonnet-4-6`, also mirrored as `providers/anthropic/models/claude-sonnet-4-6.toml` in `anomalyco/models.dev`)

```json
{ "id":"claude-sonnet-4-6","name":"Claude Sonnet 4.6","family":"claude-sonnet",
  "attachment":true,"reasoning":true,
  "reasoning_options":[{"type":"effort","values":["low","medium","high","max"]},{"type":"budget_tokens","min":1024}],
  "tool_call":true,"structured_output":true,"temperature":true,
  "knowledge":"2025-08-31","release_date":"2026-02-17","last_updated":"2026-03-13",
  "modalities":{"input":["text","image","pdf"],"output":["text"]},
  "open_weights":false,
  "limit":{"context":1000000,"output":128000},
  "cost":{"input":3,"output":15,"cache_read":0.3,"cache_write":3.75} }
```

### 5. Date/effective-pricing versioning — answers the Slack question

There **is** an explicit field: `last_updated` (plus `release_date`, `knowledge`=training cutoff) — all single ISO dates, no array/history. But it's **not a reliable price-change timestamp**: per `sync.md`, for hand-authored providers (Anthropic is TOML, manually edited) `last_updated` is bumped by whoever edits the file for *any* reason, not price specifically. For API-synced providers (OVHcloud, Chutes, etc.) the sync explicitly documents: *"`release_date`/`last_updated` default to the catalog `created` timestamp but preserve any existing hand-authored dates"* — meaning a pure price update from the API does not necessarily rewrite `last_updated` unless the sync script chooses to. **No per-field/per-price effective-date exists.** Git commit history on the TOML file in `anomalyco/models.dev` is strictly more granular than `last_updated`, but still only proves when the *models.dev contributor* edited the record, not when the provider's price actually changed. For an Entire reimplementation, recommend: store your own `price_effective_at` timestamp stamped at ingest time, don't trust `last_updated` or commit-date as ground truth.</result>

20	// RemoteCache is the on-disk shape of the cached remote pricing table. It wraps
21	// the same fileSchema the embedded models/*.json files use — so validateRate and
22	// the schema_version contract are shared, not reimplemented — with the fetch
23	// bookkeeping the background refresh needs: FetchedAt drives the 24h refresh
24	// backoff, ETag drives conditional (If-None-Match) requests, SourceURL records
25	// where the table came from for diagnostics.
26	type RemoteCache struct {
27		FetchedAt time.Time   `json:"fetched_at"`
28		ETag      string      `json:"etag,omitempty"`
29		SourceURL string      `json:"source_url,omitempty"`
30		Doc       *fileSchema `json:"doc,omitempty"`
31	}
32	
33	// remoteCacheFileName is the cache file basename. It lives beside the discovery
34	// caches under the per-user cache dir (userdirs.Cache()).
35	const remoteCacheFileName = "pricing_remote.json"
36	
37	// remoteCachePath returns the absolute path of the remote pricing cache file.
38	// Path resolution goes through userdirs.Cache — the single implementation every
39	// cache consumer shares — so the remote pricing cache sits under ~/.cache/entire
40	// (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/entire) with nodes.json and the other discovery caches.
41	func remoteCachePath() string {
42		return filepath.Join(userdirs.Cache(), remoteCacheFileName)
43	}
44	
45	// loadRemoteCache reads and parses the cache file. A missing file, a corrupt
46	// file, or any read error all return nil: the remote layer is purely additive,
47	// so "no usable cache" degrades to "embedded defaults only" and a damaged cache
48	// self-heals on the next successful refresh (which overwrites it atomically)
49	// rather than being rewritten here on the read path.
50	func loadRemoteCache() *RemoteCache {
51		data, err := os.ReadFile(remoteCachePath()) // #nosec G304 -- path derived from userdirs, not user input
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil
54		}
55		var rc RemoteCache
56		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rc); err != nil {
57			return nil
58		}
59		return &rc
60	}
61	
62	// LoadRemoteEntries returns the valid model rates from the cached remote pricing
63	// table, or nil when there is nothing usable. It is read-only and performs NO
64	// network I/O — the daily refresh (RefreshRemoteCache) is what populates the
65	// cache. It never errors: a missing or corrupt cache, an absent Doc, an
66	// unsupported schema_version, and individually invalid entries all degrade to
67	// "fewer (or zero) remote entries", so LoadPricingTable can layer whatever is
68	// valid on top of the embedded defaults without a failure path.
69	func LoadRemoteEntries(ctx context.Context) []ModelRate {
70		rc := loadRemoteCache()
71		if rc == nil || rc.Doc == nil {
72			return nil
73		}
74		if rc.Doc.SchemaVersion != 1 {
75			logging.Debug(ctx, "pricing: ignoring remote cache with unsupported schema_version",
76				slog.Int("schema_version", rc.Doc.SchemaVersion))
77			return nil
78		}
79		valid := make([]ModelRate, 0, len(rc.Doc.Models))
80		for i := range rc.Doc.Models {
81			m := rc.Doc.Models[i]
82			if err := validateRate(m); err != nil {
83				// Drop the single bad entry, keep the rest: one malformed row from
84				// the remote table must not sink the whole merge.
85				logging.Debug(ctx, "pricing: dropping invalid remote entry",
86					slog.String("id", m.ID), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
87				continue
88			}
89			valid = append(valid, m)
90		}
91		if len(valid) == 0 {
92			return nil
93		}
94		return valid
95	}
96	
97	// RemoteFetchedAt returns the time the remote pricing cache was last written, or
98	// the zero time when there is no cache. It exists for staleness diagnostics
99	// (the LoadPricingTable debug log and the manual refresh command).
100	func RemoteFetchedAt() time.Time {
101		rc := loadRemoteCache()
102		if rc == nil {
103			return time.Time{}
104		}
105		return rc.FetchedAt
106	}
107	
108	// RemoteURL is the default source for the remote pricing table. It is a var so
109	// tests can point it at an httptest server; the ENTIRE_PRICING_URL environment
110	// variable overrides it at fetch time for self-hosted setups.
111	var RemoteURL = "https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json"
112	
113	const (
114		// remoteRefreshInterval is the minimum cache age before a refresh is
115		// attempted. Every fetch outcome — success, 304, or failure — resets
116		// FetchedAt, so a broken endpoint is retried at most once per interval.
117		remoteRefreshInterval = 24 * time.Hour
118		// remoteMaxBytes caps the response body read (1 MiB), mirroring versioncheck.
119		remoteMaxBytes = 1 << 20
120	)
121	
122	// remoteFetchTimeout bounds the whole refresh request (dial + read), matching
123	// the version check's 2s budget so a slow endpoint never stalls a background
124	// worker. It is a var so tests can shrink it to exercise the timeout path fast.
125	var remoteFetchTimeout = 2 * time.Second
126	
127	// Refresh outcomes reported by RefreshResult.Outcome.
128	const (
129		refreshOutcomeUpdated     = "updated"      // 200 with a usable doc: Doc+ETag replaced.
130		refreshOutcomeNotModified = "not-modified" // 304: prior Doc kept, FetchedAt bumped.
131		refreshOutcomeUnchanged   = "unchanged"    // error/404/garbage: prior Doc kept, FetchedAt bumped.
132		refreshOutcomeSkipped     = "skipped"      // throttled: fresh cache, no request made.
133	)
134	
135	// RefreshResult summarizes what a refresh attempt did, for the manual
136	// `entire tokens pricing-refresh` report.
137	type RefreshResult struct {
138		SourceURL string
139		Outcome   string
140		Entries   int
141		FetchedAt time.Time
142		ETag      string
143	}
144	
145	// Staleness returns how old the cache is relative to now, or 0 when FetchedAt
146	// is unset.
147	func (r RefreshResult) Staleness() time.Duration {
148		if r.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
149			return 0
150		}
151		return time.Since(r.FetchedAt)
152	}
153	
154	// remoteURL returns the effective source URL, honoring the ENTIRE_PRICING_URL
155	// override read at fetch time.
156	func remoteURL() string {
157		if u := os.Getenv("ENTIRE_PRICING_URL"); u != "" {
158			return u
159		}
160		return RemoteURL
161	}
162	
163	// ShouldRefresh reports whether the remote pricing cache is stale (older than
164	// the 24h interval) or absent. Trigger sites call it to gate a background
165	// refresh spawn so a fresh cache skips the work — and the spawn — entirely.
166	func ShouldRefresh() bool {
167		rc := loadRemoteCache()
168		if rc == nil {
169			return true
170		}
171		return time.Since(rc.FetchedAt) >= remoteRefreshInterval
172	}
173	
174	// RefreshRemoteCache fetches the remote pricing table and updates the local
175	// cache, honoring the 24h throttle. It is the entry point the detached
176	// __refresh_pricing worker calls. See refreshRemoteCache for the full contract.
177	func RefreshRemoteCache(ctx context.Context) error {
178		_, err := refreshRemoteCache(ctx, false)
179		return err
180	}
181	
182	// RefreshRemoteCacheForce is RefreshRemoteCache without the freshness throttle:
183	// it always performs the network fetch and returns a RefreshResult describing
184	// the outcome. The manual `entire tokens pricing-refresh` command uses it.
185	func RefreshRemoteCacheForce(ctx context.Context) (RefreshResult, error) {
186		return refreshRemoteCache(ctx, true)
187	}
188	
189	// refreshRemoteCache is the shared implementation. It takes a cross-process
190	// flock for herd control, so several concurrently-spawned workers collapse to a
191	// single network request: the first takes the lock and refreshes, the rest take
192	// the lock, observe the freshly-written FetchedAt, and skip (unless force).
193	//
194	// Failure is absorbed, not surfaced: a network error, timeout, non-200 status,
195	// oversized/garbage body, or a doc that fails the schema/sanity check all keep
196	// the previous Doc+ETag and only bump FetchedAt — so a broken endpoint degrades
197	// to "keep serving the last good table" and is retried at most once per 24h. A
198	// 304 keeps the Doc and bumps FetchedAt. It returns an error only for a
199	// genuinely local failure (cache-dir create, lock, or write).
200	func refreshRemoteCache(ctx context.Context, force bool) (RefreshResult, error) {
201		res := RefreshResult{SourceURL: remoteURL(), Outcome: refreshOutcomeSkipped}
202	
203		// Cheap pre-lock throttle: skip the lock entirely when the cache is fresh
204		// and we are not forcing. The under-lock re-check below is the authoritative
205		// herd-control guard; this just avoids lock contention on the common path.
206		if !force && !ShouldRefresh() {
207			fillResultFromCache(&res, loadRemoteCache())
208			return res, nil
209		}
210	
211		if err := os.MkdirAll(userdirs.Cache(), 0o700); err != nil {
212			return res, fmt.Errorf("create cache dir: %w", err)
213		}
214		path := remoteCachePath()
215		release, err := flock.Acquire(path + ".lock")
216		if err != nil {
217			return res, fmt.Errorf("lock remote pricing cache: %w", err)
218		}
219		defer release()
220	
221		// Re-read under the lock. If another process refreshed while we waited for
222		// the lock, its FetchedAt is now fresh and we skip the fetch (unless forced).
223		// This is what keeps a burst of spawned workers to a single request.
224		prev := loadRemoteCache()
225		if !force && prev != nil && time.Since(prev.FetchedAt) < remoteRefreshInterval {
226			fillResultFromCache(&res, prev)
227			return res, nil
228		}
229		if prev == nil {
230			prev = &RemoteCache{}
231		}
232	
233		updated, outcome := fetchRemote(ctx, prev)
234		if err := writeRemoteCache(path, updated); err != nil {
235			return res, err
236		}
237		res.Outcome = outcome
238		fillResultFromCache(&res, updated)
239		return res, nil
240	}
241	
242	// fillResultFromCache copies the reporting fields out of a cache snapshot.
243	func fillResultFromCache(res *RefreshResult, rc *RemoteCache) {
244		if rc == nil {
245			return
246		}
247		res.FetchedAt = rc.FetchedAt
248		res.ETag = rc.ETag
249		res.Entries = countValidEntries(rc.Doc)
250	}
251	
252	// fetchRemote performs the conditional HTTP request and folds the outcome into a
253	// new RemoteCache derived from prev. Every outcome bumps FetchedAt. It never
254	// returns an error — the worst case is "keep prev's Doc+ETag".
255	func fetchRemote(ctx context.Context, prev *RemoteCache) (*RemoteCache, string) {
256		url := remoteURL()
257		out := &RemoteCache{
258			FetchedAt: time.Now(),
259			ETag:      prev.ETag,
260			SourceURL: url,
261			Doc:       prev.Doc,
262		}
263	
264		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, remoteFetchTimeout)
265		defer cancel()
266	
267		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
268		if err != nil {
269			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
270		}
271		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
272		req.Header.Set("User-Agent", versioninfo.UserAgent())
273		if prev.ETag != "" {
274			req.Header.Set("If-None-Match", prev.ETag)
275		}
276	
277		client := &http.Client{}
278		resp, err := client.Do(req)
279		if err != nil {
280			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
281		}
282		defer resp.Body.Close()
283	
284		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusNotModified {
285			return out, refreshOutcomeNotModified
286		}
287		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
288			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
289		}
290	
291		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, remoteMaxBytes))
292		if err != nil {
293			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
294		}
295		var doc fileSchema
296		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &doc); err != nil {
297			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
298		}
299		if !remoteDocUsable(&doc) {
300			return out, refreshOutcomeUnchanged
301		}
302		out.Doc = &doc
303		out.ETag = resp.Header.Get("ETag")
304		return out, refreshOutcomeUpdated
305	}
306	
307	// remoteDocUsable is the sanity gate a freshly-fetched doc must pass before it
308	// replaces the cached table: the supported schema_version and at least one entry
309	// that survives validateRate. This mirrors LoadRemoteEntries' read-time contract
310	// so a doc that would contribute zero usable rates is never stored.
311	func remoteDocUsable(doc *fileSchema) bool {
312		return countValidEntries(doc) > 0
313	}
314	
315	// countValidEntries counts the entries in doc that pass validateRate under the
316	// supported schema_version; a nil or wrong-version doc counts zero.
317	func countValidEntries(doc *fileSchema) int {
318		if doc == nil || doc.SchemaVersion != 1 {
319			return 0
320		}
321		n := 0
322		for i := range doc.Models {
323			if validateRate(doc.Models[i]) == nil {
324				n++
325			}
326		}
327		return n
328	}
329	
330	// writeRemoteCache writes rc atomically (temp + rename) so a concurrent reader
331	// never observes a half-written file.
332	func writeRemoteCache(path string, rc *RemoteCache) error {
333		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(rc, "", "  ")
334		if err != nil {
335			return fmt.Errorf("marshal remote pricing cache: %w", err)
336		}
337		tmp := path + ".tmp"
338		if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o600); err != nil {
339			return fmt.Errorf("write remote pricing cache tmp: %w", err)
340		}
341		if err := os.Rename(tmp, path); err != nil {
342			_ = os.Remove(tmp)
343			return fmt.Errorf("rename remote pricing cache: %w", err)
344		}
345		return nil
346	}

content.text:
Research is complete on all three fronts. Here's the concrete picture before I touch anything:

**What the two PRs currently do**
- **cli #1763** (`feat/cli-cost-tokens-only`, authored by you, head `433b3ce`, open, review-required): introduces a brand-new `pricing/` package (table + embedded per-provider JSON + a **daily remote-refresh overlay already pointed at `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json`, cached under `~/.cache/entire`, ETag-conditional, flock-guarded**), then explicitly **strips** the computed cost (`WithoutCost()`) before writing checkpoint metadata to disk — "platform is the source of truth."
- **entire-api #299** (`feat/platform-cost`, head `7df8251`, **explicitly marked draft — "direction change pending team sign-off"**): computes cost server-side from raw `model_usage` using its own embedded single-rate-per-model table. Its own PR body already flags the gap Soph raised in Slack — `EffectiveDate` is a single informational string, not indexed/queryable, no history — and defers the real fix to an unbuilt "Phase 3."
- **Pi's reference implementation** confirms the architecture Soph described (build-time snapshot + 4h remote overlay, staleness-guarded, forward-only) — and confirms nobody's pricing source (including models.dev) has a trustworthy price-*change* date; my research recommends stamping our own ingest-time date rather than trusting upstream ones.

**A wrinkle**: your `cli/` main checkout currently has 19 **untracked, uncommitted** files sitting on top of `main` (not on the PR branch) — the entire `pricing/` package plus matching tests, a `pricing_refresh.go` command, and settings integration. This isn't in the reflog as a recent checkout, so I can't confirm provenance, but it looks complete and already does exactly what Soph asked for in point 1 (remote catalog, daily cache, global per-machine dir). I have **not** modified or committed anything there.

**What's still missing**: `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` doesn't exist anywhere in the `entire.io` repo yet — the CLI is pointed at a URL with no backend behind it.

The one Slack point nobody pushed back on is dipree's: compute cost client-side, write it to checkpoint metadata, let the backend trust that and only estimate as a fallback for old checkpoints. That's the opposite of what both PRs currently do (#1763 strips cost; #299 always recomputes). Before I start reversing a decision embedded in two live PRs — one of which is explicitly flagged as awaiting team sign-off — I want to confirm scope with you.

This is the only reading of the thread nobody objected to.

# AGENT-COMMS.md — channel between the two Claude Code agents

Two agents work this machine in parallel:

| id | owns | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `graph-bench` | entire-graph token benchmarks, graphmark harness, rep30/rep100/300 cells | `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` |
| `memory-bench` | memory/recall benchmarks (LOCOMO, prose-memory, cmm parity) | `graph-bench-results/MemoryNotes.md` |

## Protocol

1. **Read this file at session start**, and again before touching anything in SHARED RESOURCES.
2. **Append only.** Never edit or delete another agent's entries. Newest at the bottom of the log.
3. **Claim before you touch.** Post a `CLAIM` for a shared resource before using it; post `RELEASE`
   when done. If a claim is older than 4 hours with no activity, treat it as stale and say so in
   your own entry rather than silently taking it.
4. **State evidence, not conclusions.** Every factual claim carries n, a CI or a `file:line`.
5. **Contradict freely.** If the other agent's number looks wrong, post a `CHALLENGE` with your
   re-derivation. Findings here have been wrong roughly half the time under adversarial check.

## Message format

Append a block. Keep it tight — this is a channel, not a report.

```
### [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] <from> → <to|ALL> · <TYPE>
<one-line subject>

<body: numbers, file:line, commands. 2-8 lines. no preamble.>
```

`TYPE` is one of:

| type | meaning |
|---|---|
| `CLAIM` | taking a shared resource (VM, harness file, repo branch) |
| `RELEASE` | done with it |
| `FINDING` | a result, with n and CI |
| `CHALLENGE` | disputing another agent's finding, with your re-derivation |
| `RETRACT` | withdrawing your own earlier finding, with the reason |
| `BLOCKED` | you need something the other agent owns |
| `FYI` | anything else worth knowing |

## Shared resources — claim before use

- `graphmark-bench/` harness, especially `tools/run_3arm.sh`
- GCP VMs `graphbench-a`, `-b`, `-c`, `-d` (project `graph-benchmarks-504800`)
- The Anthropic team token (rate limits are shared — say when you launch >20 concurrent sessions)
- `entireio/entire-graph` and `entirehq/graphmark` main branches

**Hard rule:** never `scp` a script onto a VM while sessions are running there. Bash reads scripts
lazily; overwriting in place corrupts live runs (22 sessions lost this way). Deploy to a temp path
then atomic `mv`.

input.description: Implement cost persistence in cli #1763
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/suhaan/devenv/pr-merge/cli-1763 (worktree of entireio/cli, branch `feat/cli-cost-tokens-only`, this IS PR #1763's actual branch, already pushed, head 433b3ceb99dfe85523c2dd88a5cae1138324a484). Work directly in this worktree, commit there. Do NOT touch /Users/suhaan/devenv/cli/ (the main checkout — it has unrelated uncommitted files, leave them alone).

## Background
PR #1763's current behavior: it computes cost in-memory for display (`EstimateCost` in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/token_usage.go`) using a new `pricing/` package (embedded per-provider JSON tables + a daily remote-refresh overlay at `pricing/remote.go`, already fetching `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json`, cached under `userdirs.Cache()`, ETag-conditional, flock-guarded — this part is solid, do not rework it) — but then explicitly STRIPS the computed cost before writing checkpoint metadata to disk via `api/checkpoint/metadata.go`'s `WithoutCost()` / `tokenUsageWithoutCost()` / `modelUsageWithoutCost()`, on the theory that "the platform is the source of truth" for cost.

A team Slack discussion (Soph, dipree, ashtom — cross-referenced with a parallel PR entirehq/entire-api#299) concluded — and nobody in the thread objected — that this is backwards: computing cost once client-side, at the moment tokens are spent, using whatever pricing was correct THEN, and persisting it into the checkpoint metadata is simpler and more historically correct than having the backend recompute cost later from raw token counts with whatever pricing table it happens to have "that day" (which breaks for forked/renamed repos with no lineage, and can't represent price changes over time without a full historical pricing table). dipree's exact words: "it's much better to do it directly on the session and write to the metadata as it reduces the complexity by a fair bit."

## Your task
1. Read `api/checkpoint/metadata.go` fully (the `WithoutCost`/`tokenUsageWithoutCost`/`modelUsageWithoutCost` functions and every call site — there are reportedly 6 write sites: git branch + refs backends, `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/fsstore/fsstore.go`, and others — grep to find them all).
2. REMOVE the stripping behavior: checkpoint metadata writes should now PRESERVE `CostUSD`/`CostSource` (both at the flat level, in nested `SubagentTokens`, and in each `ModelUsage` bucket) exactly as computed by the existing `EstimateCost`/pricing pipeline, instead of calling `WithoutCost()` before writing. The simplest correct fix is likely to delete the `WithoutCost` call sites (write the `Metadata`/`CheckpointSummary` as-is) — but read the surrounding code first; if `WithoutCost` is also used somewhere legitimately unrelated to this call path, don't break that use.
3. Decide what to do with the `WithoutCost`/`tokenUsageWithoutCost`/`modelUsageWithoutCost` functions themselves: if nothing calls them anymore after your fix, delete them (and their dedicated tests) rather than leaving dead code — check `cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go:137`'s `usageHasBillableTokens` too, since a Copilot review comment flagged it ignores `SubagentTokens` when cost estimation flattens subagents in; fix that inconsistency if it's now load-bearing (a "priced + unpriced-but-token-bearing" checkpoint should resolve to `cost_source="mixed"`, not silently drop the subagent-tokens case). Grep for `MergeCostSourceUsages` to find that logic.
4. Check the PR body / any code comments for the "legacy-checkpoint cost-stripping side effect" the author flagged (backfill/summary rewrites stripping cost from OLDER checkpoints when rewritten) — with cost no longer stripped by design, confirm this concern is now moot, and remove any now-dead special-casing for it.
5. The `EstimateCost` computation itself should remain unchanged (it's correct) — you're only changing whether the RESULT gets written to disk. Do not touch `pricing/table.go`, `pricing/remote.go`, `pricing/embed.go`, or the embedded JSON models unless you find an actual bug while reading them (if you do, fix it and say so).
6. Update/add tests: every existing test that asserted cost is ABSENT after a metadata write (search for `WithoutCost`, or assertions like `CostUSD == nil` post-write) needs to flip to assert cost IS present and correct. Add a test that a checkpoint written today, then re-read, round-trips `cost_usd`/`cost_source` unchanged.
7. Run `mise run check` (fmt + lint + test:ci) in this worktree and fix everything until it's green. This is REQUIRED before you're done — do not report success without a clean `mise run check` run. Paste the final tail of its output in your report.
8. Commit your changes with a clear, no-AI-footer commit message (repo convention: no "Co-Authored-By" / AI attribution trailers — check `git log --oneline -20` for the house style). Do NOT push — a later step handles that.

Report back CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED (dense, no prose fluff, file:line references, this feeds a downstream verification pass by another agent who will NOT re-read your work — they need the facts): what changed (file:line), what you deleted, what you fixed re: the SubagentTokens gap, exact `mise run check` tail output (pass/fail), commit SHA.

input.description: Implement reported-cost-priority in entire-api
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/suhaan/devenv/pr-merge/api-299 (worktree of entirehq/entire-api). You are on a NEW branch `feat/platform-cost-reported-priority`, created off the tip of PR #299's branch `feat/platform-cost` (head 7df8251cfdeace8ed112085482591ab8ab5a0416, which itself is a merge of main into feat/platform-cost). This is a fresh branch, not #299's actual branch — we are deliberately not pushing to #299 directly (it's marked draft, "direction change pending team sign-off", authored by app/entire bot, likely Soph's/the team's in-flight work) — instead this will become a NEW PR that supersedes/complements #299. Work directly in this worktree, commit there. Do NOT touch /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-api/ (the main checkout).

## Background
PR #299 makes entire-api compute checkpoint/session cost SERVER-SIDE from raw `model_usage` token counts, using its own embedded pricing table (`internal/pricing/models/{anthropic,openai,google,cursor}.json`, `internal/pricing/table.go`), via `estimateCost()` in `internal/ingest/cost.go` called from `parseSession` in `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go`. Critically, **the current code PARSES a CLI-supplied `cost_usd`/`cost_source` from the checkpoint metadata's model_usage entries but DISCARDS it** — always recomputing from scratch, on the stated theory "platform is the source of truth."

A companion PR to the CLI (entireio/cli#1763, being fixed in parallel right now in a different worktree) is being changed so the CLI computes cost ONCE, client-side, at session time — using whatever pricing was actually correct at that moment, via a pricing table that itself refreshes daily from a remote catalog — and PERSISTS `cost_usd`/`cost_source: "reported"` into the checkpoint metadata's `model_usage` entries (previously the CLI stripped this before writing; that's being reversed).

A team Slack discussion (Soph, dipree, ashtom) converged — unopposed — on: the backend recomputing cost from raw tokens has a real correctness problem for old/forked/renamed checkpoints (whatever pricing table exists "today" isn't necessarily what was true when the tokens were spent — no price-history mechanism exists), and it's simpler/more correct to trust a CLI-reported cost when present, and only fall back to server-side estimation for checkpoints that don't have one (legacy checkpoints from before the CLI computed cost, or checkpoints from agents/paths that never set it). dipree explicitly: "we could still do both... it's much better to do it directly on the session and write to the metadata... but [backend re-estimation as a fallback/rebuild path] still works."

## Your task
1. Read `internal/ingest/cost.go` (the `estimateCost` function) and `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go`'s `parseSession` (where it currently discards the CLI's reported cost per-model-usage-bucket, sums `estimateCost` results instead, and stamps `cost_source="estimated"`) — find the EXACT lines where the CLI-reported value is read-then-discarded.
2. Change the logic: for each `model_usage` entry, if it carries a non-nil `cost_usd` (i.e. the CLI already reported one) AND a `cost_source` indicating it was reported by the CLI, TRUST it as-is (`cost_source="reported"` on that bucket) — do not call `estimateCost`. Only call `estimateCost` (existing fallback, `cost_source="estimated"`) when the incoming bucket has no reported cost. Preserve the existing `CollapseCostSource`/multi-source aggregation logic for summing across buckets/sessions into a checkpoint-level cost + source (`"reported"`/`"estimated"`/`"mixed"`) — check `buildCheckpointRow` and `applySessionCost` in the same file, they likely need no change beyond correctly aggregating whichever per-bucket source you now set.
3. Check the goose migrations this PR added (`internal/store/migrations/repo/*_checkpoint_session_cost.sql` and `internal/store/migrations/user/*_my_activity_cost.sql` — note: this repo mandates UTC-timestamp migration filenames `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<name>.sql`, NOT hand-picked integers; confirm the ones from #299 already follow that convention post-rebase onto current main, renumber via `scripts/new-migration.sh <repo|user> <name>` if they collide with anything newly added to main) — the `cost_source` CHECK constraint currently allows `reported`/`estimated`/`mixed`; confirm `reported` is already a valid value (it should be, per the earlier research) and leave the schema alone if so.
4. This PR's own body flagged a "dual precision" issue (checkpoint `cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6)` vs per-model JSONB float, sub-cent sum mismatches) and a "cost is load-bearing on `model_usage[].model`" issue (unresolvable model → nil cost). Leave those exactly as they are UNLESS your reported-cost-priority change makes one of them meaningfully worse — if so, note it in your report, don't silently fix scope you weren't asked to touch.
5. Do NOT build any new pricing-source live-refresh mechanism here (that's explicitly out of scope — deferred as "Phase 3" in the original PR body, and a separate minimal catalog endpoint is being built in entire.io in parallel by another agent). Your ONLY job is: prefer reported cost, fall back to estimated.
6. Update/add tests in `internal/ingest/` (and `internal/store/` if checkpoint-cost persistence tests live there) covering: (a) a model_usage bucket with a reported cost is trusted verbatim and NOT recomputed even if it differs from what estimateCost would produce, (b) a bucket with no reported cost still gets estimated as before, (c) a session mixing both bucket types aggregates to `cost_source="mixed"`, (d) an unresolvable-model bucket with no reported cost still correctly yields nil cost (existing behavior, don't regress it).
7. Run `mise run build`, `mise run vet`, `mise run lint`, and `mise run test` (or the integration variant if it applies to touched packages) in this worktree. Fix everything until clean. This is REQUIRED — do not report success without clean output. Paste final tail of test output.
8. Commit with a clear message, no AI-attribution footer (check `git log --oneline -20` for house style). Do NOT push.

Report back CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED (dense, file:line, no fluff — feeds a downstream verifier who won't re-read your diff): exact before/after logic at the discard site (file:line), what you changed, migration filename check result, test results tail, commit SHA.

input.description: Build entire.io pricing-catalog endpoint
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-io-pricing (worktree of entireio/entire.io, branch `feat/pricing-catalog-endpoint`, freshly branched off `main`). Work directly in this worktree, commit there. Do NOT touch /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire.io/ (the main checkout, may hold unrelated uncommitted work).

## Background
The entireio/cli repo has an already-built, already-committed pricing-refresh mechanism (`cmd/entire/cli/pricing/remote.go` in PR #1763) that does a daily (24h), ETag-conditional, flock-guarded fetch of:

    GET https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json

...expecting a JSON body of this EXACT shape (Go struct, mirror it precisely):

```go
type fileSchema struct {
    SchemaVersion int         `json:"schema_version"`
    Models        []ModelRate `json:"models"`
}
type ModelRate struct {
    ID                string   `json:"id"`
    Provider          string   `json:"provider"`
    Aliases           []string `json:"aliases"`
    InputPerMTok      float64  `json:"input_per_mtok"`
    OutputPerMTok     float64  `json:"output_per_mtok"`
    CacheReadPerMTok  *float64 `json:"cache_read_per_mtok"`   // nullable
    CacheWritePerMTok *float64 `json:"cache_write_per_mtok"`  // nullable
    EffectiveDate     string   `json:"effective_date"`         // ISO date
}
```
(`schema_version` must be `1` — the client rejects anything else. The client also validates each entry: expects non-empty `id`/`provider`, non-negative `input_per_mtok`/`output_per_mtok`. It's forgiving of individual bad entries — drops them and keeps the rest — but the top-level fetch is only "usable" if at least one entry validates.)

This URL currently 404s (nothing serves it anywhere in the codebase) — the CLI degrades gracefully to embedded-only pricing when that happens, so this isn't blocking anyone today, but the whole point of building it is to stop the CLI's pricing from ever going stale without a release.

## Your task
1. Explore this repo's structure enough to find where to add a route. Per `api/` being the CF Workers + Hono BFF (see `api/src/index.ts` or main router, and look at how an existing simple GET JSON route is registered — e.g. something under `api/src/routes/` or wherever routes are wired — pick the smallest-blast-radius place; this endpoint has NO auth requirement, no DB access, it's a public static-ish JSON payload, so don't wire it through anything requiring Postgres/KV/auth unless the existing routing framework makes that unavoidable).
2. Write a generator script (Node/TS, following the pattern in earendil-works/pi's `packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts` — but MUCH simpler, do not port their full multi-source/override pipeline) that:
   - Fetches `https://models.dev/api.json` (single public JSON blob, all providers — no auth needed).
   - Transforms each model entry into the `ModelRate` shape above: `id` = models.dev's model id, `provider` = the provider key, `aliases` = [] (models.dev doesn't have this concept — leave empty for now), `input_per_mtok`/`output_per_mtok`/`cache_read_per_mtok`/`cache_write_per_mtok` = models.dev's `cost.input`/`cost.output`/`cost.cache_read`/`cost.cache_write` (cache fields are optional in models.dev's schema — map missing to `null`, do NOT synthesize a value), `effective_date` = **the date this script ran** (today, in ingest-time UTC ISO date form, e.g. `2026-08-10`) — NOT models.dev's `last_updated` field. This is an intentional, important decision: research shows `last_updated` in models.dev is unreliable as a price-change date (it's bumped by any edit, not just price edits, for hand-authored providers) — do not use it, use ingest time, and add a one-line comment explaining why (cite: models.dev's own sync docs don't guarantee last_updated tracks price changes specifically).
   - Writes the output as `{schema_version: 1, models: [...]}` to a file this repo can serve (e.g. `api/src/generated/pricing-models.json`, or wherever fits the repo's existing static-asset convention — check for precedent).
   - Include basic sanity gates before writing (mirroring Pi's `validateBundle` spirit but minimal): reject if fewer than ~50 total models parsed, reject if `anthropic` or `openai` provider keys are entirely absent — fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear stderr message) rather than writing a garbage file.
3. Wire a route (`GET /pricing/v1/models.json` — must resolve at exactly this path under whatever the `entire.io` prod domain routing is, check `wrangler.toml`/routing config for how `/pricing/*` would map, since the CLI hits the bare domain `entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` not `api.entire.io/...` — find out which worker/route currently owns unauthenticated bare-domain paths and slot in there; if the bare domain routes through a different worker than `api/` (e.g. the frontend CF Worker or a dedicated redirects config), say so and put the route in the CORRECT place, don't guess) that serves the generated JSON file's current contents, with:
   - `Content-Type: application/json`
   - An `ETag` header (content hash of the served body) so the CLI's conditional `If-None-Match` requests get real 304s.
   - A reasonable `Cache-Control` (this is safe to cache aggressively at the edge since it only changes when the generator reruns — e.g. `public, max-age=3600` — but must still return fresh ETags after regeneration).
4. Add a way to regenerate the file (a package.json script, e.g. `generate:pricing-catalog`, calling your generator) — do NOT wire it into the main build pipeline yet (no CI cron/action — that's explicitly a follow-up the team hasn't decided on: manual/on-demand regen for now is fine, note this limitation clearly in your report and in a code comment at the route).
5. Write tests: the generator's transform logic (given a sample models.dev-shaped fixture, produces correct ModelRate entries, correctly nulls missing cache fields, correctly stamps today's date not models.dev's date, correctly rejects too-few-models), and the route (serves valid JSON matching the schema, sets ETag, honors If-None-Match with a 304, unauthenticated request succeeds).
6. Run this repo's test commands (`mise run test`, `mise run api-test` — whichever covers the code you touched) until clean. This is REQUIRED.
7. Commit with a clear message, no AI-attribution footer (check `git log --oneline -20` for house style in this repo). Do NOT push.

Report back CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED (dense, file:line, no fluff — feeds a downstream verifier): exact route path + which worker owns it and why, generator file location, sample of one transformed entry, test results tail (pass/fail), commit SHA, and explicitly flag the manual-regen limitation and any assumption you had to make about bare-domain routing.

input.message:
An independent skeptic re-verified your work in /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-io-pricing and found two real, blocking defects in the generator's data, not the routing/serving code (which it confirmed is correct). Fix these before we push:

1. **Payload exceeds the CLI's read cap → feature silently no-ops.** The CLI (`cmd/entire/cli/pricing/remote.go:119`) caps the response body read at `remoteMaxBytes = 1 << 20` (1 MiB) via `io.LimitReader`. Your committed `pricing-models.json` is 1,561,781 bytes (1.49 MiB) — so every real fetch gets truncated, `json.Unmarshal` fails, and the refresh silently falls back to "unchanged" forever. This needs to comfortably fit under 1 MiB.

2. **Root cause, and the actual bug to fix: models.dev is keyed by (provider, model), your transform flattens to a flat id-keyed array with no dedup/qualification.** There are 896 duplicate model ids across 172 providers in models.dev (563 of which have DIVERGENT prices between providers — same model id, different $ depending on which reseller/aggregator serves it). Your current code just lets whichever entry comes last for a given id win. The CLI's own `Table.add()` (in cli's pricing/table.go) is ALSO last-wins keyed by lowercased id, and OVERWRITES the `Provider` field too — so if you just shrink the payload by truncating/sampling without fixing this, you can hand the CLI wildly wrong pricing. The skeptic proved this concretely: `claude-sonnet-4-6` resolved to provider `xpersona` instead of `anthropic`, at $10.29/MTok instead of the correct $22.05 (input+output combined) — a 53% understatement — and `claude-opus-4-1` resolved to provider `requesty`, which silently breaks the CLI's Anthropic-specific cache-rate multiplier fallback (that fallback only applies `if provider == "anthropic"`).

FIX: Filter the catalog to first-party/canonical providers only before building the id-keyed array — i.e. only include entries where models.dev's provider key IS the actual model vendor (anthropic, openai, google, etc.), NOT resellers/aggregators/gateways that re-list the same model id under their own provider key (xpersona, requesty, cortecs, 302ai, daoxe, and similar aggregator provider keys should be EXCLUDED). The skeptic measured that a first-party-only slice is ~381 entries / ~102 KB — comfortably under the 1 MiB cap with huge margin. After filtering, ALSO verify zero duplicate ids remain (the skeptic found 58 dupe ids even within a naive first-party filter — you'll need to actually check provider-by-provider which one is canonical, e.g. don't just filter by a hardcoded allowlist and assume that's sufficient, verify the resulting id set has no collisions, and if a genuine collision remains between two first-party providers for the same id — shouldn't happen but verify — resolve it explicitly rather than silently last-wins).

Also: zero-priced upstream subscription-style entries pass your validation (guard is only `< 0`, so `0` slips through) — decide whether $0 is ever legitimately correct (e.g. a genuinely free tier) vs. upstream data noise, and tighten the guard if the latter.

Do NOT touch the routing/serving code (app.ts, wrangler.jsonc, pricing.ts route, ETag/304 logic) — the skeptic confirmed all of that is correct and well-tested. This is purely a generator/data-transform fix in api/src/lib/pricing/catalog.ts + regenerating pricing-models.json via your existing generate-pricing-catalog.ts script. Update/add tests proving: (a) no duplicate ids in the final catalog, (b) known aggregator provider keys are excluded, (c) the regenerated file size is well under 1 MiB, (d) claude-sonnet-4-6 resolves to provider="anthropic" with the correct $3/$15 input/output rates (matching live models.dev's anthropic entry specifically, not some other provider's).

Re-run the full test suite + tsc + oxlint clean, amend your existing commit (9995b471b8, not yet pushed — safe to amend), and report back CAVEMAN-ULTRA COMPRESSED: final catalog size in bytes, final model count, exact provider allowlist/exclusion logic used, confirmation of zero duplicate ids, the claude-sonnet-4-6 spot check, test results tail.

## Summary

Stands up `GET /pricing/v1/models.json` — the endpoint the CLI's pricing-refresh mechanism (entireio/cli#1763) already expects at `https://entire.io/pricing/v1/models.json` but which doesn't exist anywhere yet, so the CLI currently degrades silently to its embedded pricing snapshot.

This is the "Pi method" approach discussed in the team Slack thread on entirehq/entire-api#299 / entireio/cli#1763: an embedded baseline shipped with the CLI, plus a background overlay refreshed from our own hosted catalog (rather than depending on Pi/pi.dev directly), sourced the same way Pi sources theirs — from `models.dev`.

- Route registered on the `entire-io-api` Worker (exact-path carve-out on the `entire.io` zone, same mechanism as the existing `/auth/*`, `/api/v1/*`, `/.well-known/entire-api.json` carve-outs — Cloudflare route matching prefers the more specific pattern over the frontend Worker's `entire.io/*` catch-all, verified against Cloudflare's documented routing precedence).
- `Content-Type: application/json`, content-hash `ETag`, real `304` on matching `If-None-Match`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, no auth required.
- Generator (`api/scripts/generate-pricing-catalog.ts`) pulls live from `models.dev/api.json`, filters to first-party model vendors only (anthropic, openai, google, xai, meta, mistral, cohere, deepseek, and a few others), and hard-fails (throws) on any duplicate model id surviving the filter — models.dev lists many of the same model ids under dozens of reseller/aggregator provider keys at different prices, so an unfiltered flatten would hand the CLI wrong-provider, wrong-price data.
- `effective_date` is stamped at ingest time (today), not copied from models.dev's own `last_updated` field — that field isn't a reliable price-change signal (bumped by any edit to hand-authored provider files, not just price edits).
- Committed catalog: 218 models, 57 KB (well under the CLI's 1 MiB fetch cap).

**Known limitation, intentionally left as follow-up**: regeneration is manual (`pnpm generate:pricing-catalog`), not wired into CI/build yet — the team hasn't settled on an automated refresh cadence/ownership model for this.

## Test plan
- [x] Full `vitest.unit.config.ts` suite green (204 files / 4007 tests)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean, `oxlint` clean
- [x] Route tested end-to-end through the real Hono app (200 + schema + ETag + genuine 304)
- [x] Generator tested for: aggregator-provider exclusion, zero-duplicate-id invariant, correct `claude-sonnet-4-6` → `anthropic` resolution
- [x] Verified end-to-end against the real `entire` CLI binary: fetched over HTTP, parsed, accepted all 218 entries with zero rejections
EOF
)"

cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/pr-merge/api-299
gh pr create --repo entirehq/entire-api \
  --title "fix(cost): trust CLI-reported cost, fall back to server estimate" \
  --head feat/platform-cost-reported-priority \
  --base feat/platform-cost \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Builds on #299, addressing the team Slack discussion (Soph/dipree/ashtom) on that PR: computing cost server-side from raw `model_usage` has a real correctness problem for old/forked/renamed checkpoints, since it always uses whatever pricing table exists "today," with no history. The unopposed conclusion in that thread was to trust a cost computed once, client-side, at session time (now landing in entireio/cli#1763) and persisted into checkpoint metadata — and have the platform trust that reported value, falling back to server-side estimation only when it's absent (legacy checkpoints, or paths that never set one).

- `internal/ingest/cost.go`: new `bucketCost`/`reportedCost` — a well-formed reported cost (`cost_source="reported"`, passes `ValidCostUSD`, including a genuine `$0`) is trusted verbatim; `estimateCost` is now purely the fallback.
- `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go` `parseSession`: both `model_usage` buckets and aggregate `token_usage` now go through the same trust-then-fallback path, so the two payload shapes can't disagree. Existing `CollapseCostSource` aggregation (`reported`/`estimated`/`mixed`) is unchanged.
- Does **not** add any pricing-source live-refresh mechanism (that's out of scope here — see entirehq/entire.io#3643 for the client-side catalog piece, and #299's own "Phase 3" note).

## Two bugs found in #299 itself while building this, unrelated to the feature above

Both reproduced against a real Postgres, not just from reading the diff — flagging regardless of what happens with this PR, since #299 is still marked draft/pending sign-off and either would break things badly if merged as-is:

1. **`internal/store/store.go` `UpsertMyActivity`** listed 28 columns against a `VALUES` clause with only `$1..$26` — **every** `my_activity` write (not just cost-related ones) fails with `SQLSTATE 42601`. Fixed here (`93e6f9ee`).
2. **The two goose migrations #299 added** (`checkpoint_session_cost`, `my_activity_cost`) used hand-picked integer filenames instead of this repo's mandated UTC-timestamp format, and `main` has since advanced past those integers. Confirmed on a real Postgres: goose hard-errors ("detected 1 missing (out-of-order) migration") rather than silently skipping, so the service **fails to boot** in any already-migrated environment. Renamed to timestamped filenames here (`2ee670bf`). Also worth noting: this repo's own migration docs describe goose as silently skipping out-of-order migrations — that's incorrect for the `Provider` API version in use (v3.27.1) and should probably be corrected separately.

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run build` / `vet` / `lint` / `test` all clean
- [x] New tests: reported cost trusted verbatim (even when it disagrees with what `estimateCost` would produce), estimate-fallback when absent, mixed-source aggregation, unresolvable-model + no-reported-cost still yields nil (no regression), unusable reported values (wrong label/negative/non-finite) fall back to estimate correctly
- [x] Integration suite run against a real Postgres (embedded, no Docker): store + httpapi + sessionname + importer all green
- [x] Migration rename verified live: pre-fix filenames fail to apply against current `main`'s migration state; renamed versions apply cleanly
EOF
)"

content.text: Confirmed — `CostSourceReported` is set by the CLI only for the rare case where the agent itself reports real billed dollars (e.g. Cursor's own billing). For the common case (Claude Code and most agents), the CLI computes cost from tokens and labels it `"estimated"` — which is still a genuine, spend-time-correct, CLI-computed value that should be trusted. entire-api's current logic wrongly treats that as "nothing reported" and silently re-estimates. This is a real bug, not a nuance I'm misreading. Fixing it now.

activity forward as tokens, but no scenario in this suite ever set a
cost on the forwarded checkpoint, so a break in that wiring — or in
either of its two independent sanitize layers (egress in
ingest.CheckpointActivityEvent, consumer-side in
forwarder.Consumer.onEvent) — would have passed silently. Adds the
happy path and the untrusted-input sanitize path; mutation-verified
(removing either sanitize layer alone still passes, since each is
