input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/suhaan/devenv/pr-merge/cli-1763 (entireio/cli worktree, branch feat/cli-cost-tokens-only, currently HEAD is our commit c105d41ed on top of PR #1763's history — do not worry about PR mechanics, just fix code and commit locally, do not push). This is a real, high-confidence (0.75) bug found by an automated review pass on this PR, plus a related medium-severity finding in the same functions. Both need fixing with mutation-verified tests before this PR can be considered done.

## Bug #1 (High severity): unbounded additive inflation of subagent cost/tokens across a multi-turn session

Location: the interaction between `cmd/entire/cli/agent/token_usage.go` (`CalculateUsageWithCost` at line ~63, `remainderBucket` at line ~318, `flattenTokenUsage` at line ~348) and `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_git.go` (`accumulateTokenUsage` ~line 355, `accumulateModelUsage` ~line 408).

Mechanism (I've already traced this fully, don't re-derive it, just confirm and fix):
- `CalculateUsageWithCost` is called once per turn-end (`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1012`), scoped to a transcript delta window via `fromOffset`.
- The returned `flat.SubagentTokens` subtree is a **cumulative-since-session-start snapshot**, NOT a per-turn delta — this is documented behavior (see the comment above `accumulateTokenUsage` in manual_commit_git.go: "Subagent usage arrives as a cumulative-since-session-start snapshot... re-reads each subagent transcript from its start on every call"). This is WHY `accumulateTokenUsage` deliberately REPLACES `existing.SubagentTokens` each turn instead of adding it (line ~396: `existing.SubagentTokens = accumulateTokenUsage(nil, incoming.SubagentTokens)`) — that part is correct and already handles the cumulative snapshot right.
- BUT `remainderBucket` (token_usage.go:318) computes `flattenTokenUsage(flat)` — which flattens `flat`'s own (correctly per-turn-delta-scoped) top-level scalar fields TOGETHER WITH the full recursive `SubagentTokens` subtree (cumulative, NOT delta-scoped) — into one number, then subtracts `sum(buckets)` (the main-agent per-model buckets, which ARE correctly per-turn-delta-scoped) to get a "shortfall" bucket under `fallbackModel`. Since the subagent portion of that flattened number is cumulative (not delta), the shortfall each turn is dominated by close to the FULL cumulative subagent total, not just the NEW subagent tokens since the last turn.
- That remainder bucket then gets `buckets = append(buckets, rem)` and flows out of `CalculateUsageWithCost` as part of the returned `buckets` slice.
- At the accumulation layer, `accumulateModelUsage` (manual_commit_git.go:408) folds each turn's buckets into a running `map[string]*agent.TokenUsage` keyed by model, via `accumulateTokenUsage(existing[model], &bucket)` — which ADDS scalar fields (correct for genuine per-turn-delta buckets from the main agent, WRONG for the remainder bucket since its contribution is derived from a cumulative-not-delta quantity).
- Net effect: for any multi-turn session with subagents, each subsequent turn's remainder bucket re-reports close to the full cumulative subagent total again, and that gets ADDED on top of every previous turn's already-large remainder — `state.TokenUsage.CostUSD`, `state.CheckpointTokenUsage.CostUSD`, and `state.ModelUsage` inflate without bound as the session progresses, even if actual subagent activity is flat or small after the first turn.

## What NOT to do
- Do not change how `SubagentTokens` itself is accumulated (replace-not-add) — that's correct as-is.
- Do not change how genuine per-turn main-agent model-usage buckets accumulate (add-across-turns) — that's correct for them; only the remainder bucket's cumulative-subagent-derived contribution is wrong.
- Do not just clamp/cap the remainder bucket ad hoc — find the actual root cause fix: the remainder bucket must reflect only the NEW subagent tokens since the last time a remainder was computed for this session/checkpoint accumulation scope, not the full cumulative snapshot.

## Your task for Bug #1
1. Read the full call chain yourself to confirm my trace (I'm confident in it, but verify before you commit to a design — especially confirm whether `flat`'s top-level scalar fields really are per-turn-delta-scoped by the time they reach `remainderBucket`, since that assumption is load-bearing for the fix).
2. Design and implement a fix that makes the remainder bucket's contribution correctly delta-scoped across turns, consistent with how `SubagentTokens` itself and the main per-model buckets are each correctly handled today. Likely shape: thread a "previously-accounted-for cumulative subagent snapshot" into `CalculateUsageWithCost`/`remainderBucket` (sourced from the running session/checkpoint state that already tracks the previous turn's cumulative `SubagentTokens`, e.g. `state.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens` or `state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens` in the strategy layer — check both, since there may be two independently-accumulated aggregates that each need their own correct baseline), and subtract that baseline before computing the shortfall, so the remainder only reflects the NEW increment. There may be a cleaner design than passing yet another parameter through several functions — use your judgment, but keep the fix as small and locally-reasoned as the existing code's style (extensive doc comments explaining WHY, matching the existing file's voice).
3. Consider: is there a risk that `state.TokenUsage` and `state.CheckpointTokenUsage` (two separately-accumulated aggregates per the "Token usage scoping" note in this repo's CLAUDE.md: TokenUsage is session-wide, CheckpointTokenUsage is the pending-checkpoint-delta-since-last-condensation) need DIFFERENT baselines, since they reset/reference different windows? Get this right — a wrong baseline for one of them while fixing the other would just move the bug rather than fix it.

## Bug #2 (Medium severity): CacheCreation1hTokens dropped, silently undercounting 1h-cache-TTL cost

Location: `remainderBucket` (token_usage.go:318) builds its `short` TokenUsage from only `InputTokens`/`CacheCreationTokens`/`CacheReadTokens`/`OutputTokens`/`APICallCount` — never `CacheCreation1hTokens`. `flattenTokenUsage` (token_usage.go:348) has the same gap when flattening `flat`/`u.SubagentTokens`. Net effect: any cache-creation tokens attributed through the remainder path, or through `EstimateCost`'s flat fallback, get billed entirely at the 5-minute cache-write rate (1.25x) instead of the 2x 1-hour rate for sessions using 1h cache TTL — a silent cost undercount.

Fix: add `CacheCreation1hTokens` to both `flattenTokenUsage`'s recursive summation and `remainderBucket`'s `sum`/`short` construction (check whether `buckets[i].TokenUsage` already carries `CacheCreation1hTokens` from `modelUsageBuckets`/`bucketTokens` — if `bucketTokens` also drops it, that's a related gap to fix too, check `bucketTokens` at token_usage.go around line 383).

## Verification (REQUIRED, do not skip)
1. Write a test that simulates a multi-turn session with subagent activity where subagent tokens are LARGE on turn 1 and STAY ROUGHLY FLAT on turns 2 and 3 (i.e., `flat.SubagentTokens`'s flattened total is ~unchanged turn-over-turn) — assert that the ACCUMULATED cost/tokens after 3 turns is NOT roughly 3x the correct single-turn total (which is what the bug produces) but stays close to the correct cumulative total. Mutation-verify: revert your fix and confirm this test fails with inflated (roughly N-times-too-large) values.
2. Write a test proving `CacheCreation1hTokens` now survives `flattenTokenUsage` and `remainderBucket`'s shortfall computation and gets billed at the 2x rate, not 1.25x. Mutation-verify similarly.
3. Run the FULL existing test suite for the affected packages (`go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/... ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/...` at minimum) to confirm no regressions — pay special attention to any existing tests asserting specific cost/token totals across multi-turn scenarios, since your fix changes real accumulation behavior.
4. Run `mise run check` (fmt + lint + full test:ci, including the Vogon e2e canary) in this worktree. This is REQUIRED — do not report done without a clean run. This repo's CLAUDE.md requires `mise run fmt && mise run lint` to both be clean AND re-run lint if fmt changed anything.
5. Commit your changes locally with a clear message (no AI-attribution footer — check `git log --oneline -20` for house style). Do NOT push — a separate step handles that.

Same missing-resanitization issue as `buildCheckpointRow` in `internal/ingest/checkpoint.go`: `costSum` is the sum of already-validated per-checkpoint costs, but the sum itself is never re-checked against `ValidCostUSD` before being stored as `row.costUSD`, which is written to the `sessions.cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6)` column. `costSum` here is written straight to `cp.CostUSD` and flows to the `checkpoints.cost_usd NUMERIC(14,6)` column via `UpsertCheckpoint`, but it is never re-validated with `store.ValidCostUSD`/`SanitizeCost` after summing. Each per-session cost is checked individually, but a checkpoint with several sessions whose valid (each `< 1e8`) costs sum to `>= 1e8` will overflow the column on INSERT — exactly the poison-redelivery failure mode `ValidCostUSD`'s own doc warns about. Compare with `applySessionCost` just below, which does call `store.SanitizeCost(&sum, ...)` on its aggregate before storing it — this aggregation path is missing the equivalent guard.
